name: Ameris Bank Jacksonville Marathon
summary: The Ameris Bank Jacksonville Marathon is a flat, fast Boston-qualifying race held in December. It starts at the Bolles School, heads south into Mandarin and loops back along the St. Johns River. A race listing says there are no hills, bridges or overpasses and that about 85% of the route is shaded.
courseHighlights: Start at the Bolles School on San Jose Boulevard
Return along the St. Johns River

paceStrategy.summary: With no hills, bridges or overpasses, the course suits even pacing. The shade helps in warm weather, but Florida can be humid, so drink early.

segments.terrain: Flat roads south from the Bolles School; the half marathon splits off near mile 7
segments.advice: Hold goal pace and settle into a rhythm.
Keep the effort even and take fluids at each aid station.

segments.terrain: Return along the St. Johns River
segments.advice: Stay steady; there are no hills, so hold form.

fuelingNotes: A race listing says water stations are about every 2 miles. Carry your own gels and plan to take one about every 45 minutes.
tips: The race starts and finishes at the Bolles School, so parking and logistics are in one place
Wear light layers: December mornings in Florida can start cool and warm up
The course is mostly shaded, so sunglasses are less needed but a cap helps if it warms up
Check the current sponsor and date on the official race page; the name has changed over the years

faq.question: Is the Jacksonville Marathon flat?
faq.answer: Yes. A race listing calls the profile very flat, with no hills, bridges or overpasses.

faq.question: When is the Jacksonville Marathon held?
faq.answer: It is held on a Saturday in December.

faq.question: Where does the Jacksonville Marathon start?
faq.answer: It starts at the Bolles School in Jacksonville and heads south into Mandarin.
